review_cost.rationale: Approve after a round of nits: none are architectural, and each has an obvious in-place fix. The spec-sensitive parts (URL state, sort semantics, coverage math) are correct and well-factored.

findings.issue: The server-only data module (env access, fetch, global cache) is not named *.server.ts, so TanStack Start's import protection can't block a future client-side import; pure helpers like englishName/idFromUrl/collapse live in it and are tempting to reuse from components.
findings.suggestion: Rename to pokeapi.server.ts (matches the default '**/*.server.*' rule) and move pure helpers into lib/format.ts so the boundary is enforced by the build.

findings.issue: No route defines an errorComponent, so any non-404 upstream failure (e.g. 500 from the API) surfaces as the router's default error UI, and fetchJson has no timeout, letting a hung upstream block SSR indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Add a defaultErrorComponent to createRouter and an AbortSignal/timeout in fetchJson.

findings.issue: getPokemonById(species.id) is the only resource fetch not wrapped in orNull; a species with no default Pokémon yields an unhandled loader error instead of the Not found page the rest of the app produces.
findings.suggestion: Use `const pokemon = await orNull(getPokemonById(species.id)); if (!pokemon) return null`.

findings.issue: writeTeamCookie is called inside the setState updater, making the updater impure; React StrictMode double-invokes it and any future refactor (logging, batching) could double-apply side effects.
findings.suggestion: Compute the next team outside the updater (or write the cookie in an effect keyed on `team`).

findings.issue: The root head sniffs the private `m._notFound` field to render the not-found title, which is undocumented and can break on upgrades.
findings.suggestion: Rely on `m.status === 'notFound'` only, or set the title from the notFoundComponent side via a dedicated not-found route head.

findings.issue: Row keys `${row.move}-${row.level}` collide when a move appears more than once for the same version group and method (PokeAPI does contain such duplicates).
findings.suggestion: Key on the row's index within the built rows array.

findings.issue: The type-label Map construction is duplicated verbatim in routes/index.tsx:63 and routes/team.tsx:20.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small `useTypeLabels(types)` helper next to PokemonCardList.

findings.issue: The home page ships the entire 1,025-entry species index (with types and generation) through the loader into the SSR/hydration payload (~100 KB of JSON per page load) — justified by the instant-search requirement, but worth being deliberate about.
findings.suggestion: Keep the approach but note the payload cost in a comment, or gate future growth (e.g. more per-entry fields) behind a server-filtered variant.

findings.issue: A Pokémon page fans out one move fetch per learnable move (~90-150 requests, all cached for 60s) plus one per version group, which is inherent to PokeAPI's shape but makes page latency depend on cache warmth.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is given the snapshot API and the shared TTL cache; consider longer TTLs for immutable data if it becomes hot.

findings.issue: 'config.ts' contains a single useMediaBase hook, not configuration; the name misleads when searching for app settings.
findings.suggestion: Rename to lib/useMediaBase.ts (or merge into lib/format's callers).

summary: A textbook TanStack Start app: current APIs (validator-based server functions, head/meta, notFound, srvx prod server), clean file-based routes, and a server layer that reads like a BFF. The risks are minor and mostly at the edges: an under-enforced server/client boundary (pokeapi.ts not *.server.ts), no custom error handling, and one impure setState updater. I'd merge after a round of small fixes.
